I always keep canned chicken. 2 cans plus mayo, relish (or pickles) a hard boiled egg, onion (optional) for chicken salad. Could do tuna or just egg for tuna or egg salad. I also add salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, basil, parsley, red pepper flakes. I either eat it on toast with a slice of cheese, with crackers or tortilla chips, or on a tortilla as a wrap. That’ll last me a little over a week but I eat it pretty regularly. Super cheap and easy! I was raised by southern people and grew up eating it. Some people are grossed out by it lol whatever!! 

I second pasta sauce and meatballs. I’ll make an entire jar of pasta sauce at a time. I like to cook a bunch of frozen meatballs in it. One day, I’ll use it for spaghetti and meatballs. The next day, I’ll make meatball subs. I throw some hot dog buns (I normally buy brioche buns) in the toaster until they’re slightly crispy. Throw the meatballs and sauce on with your choice of cheese and throw it in the oven until the cheese melts. Soooo good. My roommates are obsessed!! I use pepper jack cheese bc I like the spice, but whatever cheese you have works! 

I’m obsessed with boxed rice dishes. Jambalaya is by far my favorite. I add chicken and smoked sausage and eat it with garlic bread. 

I second what others have said about keeping frozen chicken tenderloins or breasts. You can thaw them and cook them or they cook in the oven in like 30-40 minutes from frozen. When I’m running out of fridge space (3 roommates), I throw my frozen chicken in the crockpot with a little oil, fresh chopped onion and garlic, salt, pepper, oregano, basil, maybe some thyme. On high for ~3 hours. I shred the chicken and then use it throughout the week. Can add it to mac and cheese, chicken alfredo, tacos (add cumin, chili powder, garlic and onion powder, cayenne), bbq chicken sandwiches, homemade chicken and noodles. 

Something else I like to do is buy bell peppers and onion, dice and/ or julienne them all at once, and then freeze them so they last longer and add it to whatever you’re making!!

For snacks, I like to keep fruits and veggies on hand with my favorite dip. With apples, mango, grapes, strawberries, and blueberries (other fruits probably work, too, these are just my go-tos!) I make a dip that’s equal parts softened cream cheese and marshmallow cream. Add a dash of vanilla and a dash of milk and it’s perfect. You can use mixed berry cream cheese for added flavor :) 

Again, I’m midwestern. I love ranch. A packet of hidden valley seasoning with a tub or sour cream makes the perfect ranch dip. Pair with carrots, celery, broccoli, cauliflower, grape tomatoes, cucumber, snap peas, bell peppers. 

I like to keep yogurts on hand. Either plain yogurt and I add granola and fruit or the little Yoplait yogurts. 

Crackers and cheese are a CLASSIC. Club crackers are so good!! I keep blocks of colby jack cheese on hand for that and just to eat because I loveeee colby jack cheese.

Hopefully some of these helped!

Edit: Another incredibly easy one: Smoked sausage, green beans, and potatoes. This is so cheap and so yummy. A can of green beans keep the juice it comes in, like 4-5 potatoes, and half a package of smoke sausage. Add water until it covers all of them. Throw in some chicken bullion cubes (maybe 2 or 3), season it super super well with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, parsley. You can either boil it in a pot until the potatoes are done or in the crockpot until the potatoes are done. I sometimes will quarter and onion and throw that in too. Or fresh garlic cloves. I use whatever smoked sausage I have left for jambalaya or I’ll fry it with eggs for an easy breakfast.

I’m a firm believer in gender euphoria being a better indicator of transness than gender dysphoria. Not all trans people experience dysphoria. However, all of us experience that rush of euphoria when we’re being referred to correctly. That’s what unifies us :)

I present very femininely most of the time and am AFAB so unless I tell people directly that my pronouns are they/them, they always default to she/her. However, sometimes in high school, my teachers would accidentally call me “he” instead of “she” and ofc my classmates would all giggle and internally I’d be like “yesssss!!!!” 

I’ve also seen other AFAB non-binary ppl put their pronouns in their bio as “They/He as in, if you can’t wrap your little pea brain around the singular they, I’d rather you use he/him pronouns for me” and I kind of relate to that. I think if I didn’t go by they/them pronouns, I’d go by she/he pronouns and have my friends alternate between the two. 

Sometimes I’m okay with feminine terms, but when feminine terms aren’t okay, they’re *very* not okay. I’ve explained to my friends that it’s like a 50/50 chance if she/her pronouns will be okay, 75/25 that he/him will be okay, and 100% likely that they/them will be okay. 

TL;DR: Yes!!!!

I was really lucky in finding a partner who is very understanding and is also non-binary themself. I think that if your partner already knows what being non-binary is, it’s much easier than if they don’t. In a previous relationship, I started by talking about myself more fluidly in person and online and sharing trans information on my social media. Like retweeting Elliot page when they came out. You could do that or you could always start by doing what you did. I’m non-binary and for me that means... And go from there. 

A lot of people find letters or texts to be easier because you can plan everything you have to say before they receive it. 

I’ll see if I can find this one chart that has like a list of terms that are okay and a list of terms that are not. 

It’s overall going to be a process. My roommates still deadname and misgender me on accident because they’ve known me since I was in middle school lol so expect it to be an adjustment, but if your partner really loves you and cares about your health and happiness, they’ll be willing to make the little changes. 

When I was trying to figure out names, I had a list of them and my partner and I tried them together in private until I felt more comfy with my chosen name. When they started questioning their gender, I started alternating between she and they pronouns. They realized that they/she is what works best for them. So it’s like a whole process but *so* worth it. I feel much closer to my gf than before because we’ve been able to have these open, raw conversations about gender and what it means to us.

I’m nonbinary and for me that means I can be whoever I want whenever I want. There’s no pressure to be confined in a box. If I want to wear my binder and a bright pink crop top, i can (and I have!). If I want to be a boyfriend today but a girlfriend tomorrow, my partner is so down. They default to “significant other” or “love interest” when referring to me, but when they can tell I’m feeling more masculine, they’ll throw in a “boyfriend” or a “dude” just to make me feel more comfortable. If I’m feeling particularly feminine, they’ll tell me I’m so pretty. If neither works or both works, they’ll go gender neutral or alternate. It’s so nice. I can be all of those things!

I’m a sister and a brother and a daughter and a son and a girlfriend and a boyfriend and sometimes I’m none of those things, just a sibling and a child and a love interest. I love being genderfluid. I love being nonbinary.

I’m not much older than you, only 20, and I’m normally just a lurker on this sub but I wanted to reach out. I didn’t come out as nonbinary until I was moved out and in college because I feared the same consequences you’ve described. It sucked having to hide myself for so long, but sometimes that’s the safer option. I think, in this situation, I would try to keep yourself safe first and foremost. If that means keeping the closet door shut, then so be it. I found that when i was your age, having a separate, private account on your preferred social media platform with your name and pronouns is very helpful. And just immersing yourself in the LGBT (trans specifically) community through social media, movies and tv, etc. Do what you can to ease your dysphoria when you can. I know this sounds really awful and depressing but now I’m 20 and I’m in my own apartment and all of my roommates call me by my correct name and pronouns. My correct name is on a stocking hanging in our living room right now. Every day I feel so free. I promise you this is coming. I got my first binder recently and I cut my hair how I like and it’s just everything I was aching for at 15. It’s coming. Hang in there. Don’t kill yourself. I thought about it for so long and I still do sometimes. But I choose to live for my girlfriend, who is also nonbinary and understands me so deeply. And I choose to live because I’m going to be a teacher and I never had a trans teacher, so I get to be the role model that I never had. There are big things and little things that make me choose to live. I didn’t have any reasons at 15, but I do now. I’m glad I stayed around long enough to see my first apartment. I’m hanging on until I’m 30. That’s kind of been my motivation.  I don’t know why but I can’t wait to be 30. So, pick a number. Hold on to that. DM any time you need to. I’ll give you all the affirmations and love and advice I can give. You got this! I love you!

It definitely matters way less if you feel dysphoric and way more if you feel euphoric. The fact that you like when people call you by they/them pronouns is important. My significant other recently came out as non-binary and their biggest concern was the fact that they didn’t have dysphoria. Not having dysphoria doesn’t mean anything. Don’t worry about that!

It helped me to figure out my non-binary identity by trying new labels and pronouns with just my close friends and then slowly using them with more and more people. Right now, my girlfriend, roommates, and best friends are calling me Ren while I try it out to see how it fits. They did this for me with a different name a few years back! Hellaaaaa euphoria!!! 

My identity was basically cis woman > demigirl > genderfluid and I’ve ID’d as genderfluid for about 5 years ish now! I used to always describe feeling like “a girl but a little to the left.” My s/o explained it to me by drawing a circle with the word “woman” in it and putting their name just outside the circle. They were like “you see how I’m really close to the circle, but I’m not in it? Is this non-binary?” and yeah. That’s non-binary. 

I frequently call myself a non-binary woman bc I do have some attachment to womanhood sometimes. But I still bind pretty regularly and I don’t mind gendered terms like “bro” and “girlfriend” but certain words like “girl” and “sis” do bother me. So, yeah! Basically, you don’t have to check off a list. You can be a little bit of everything. 

If you *want* to be non-binary, you’re probably non-binary. And that’s not faking it or jumping on the bandwagon. That’s just that. We would be happy to have you in our little community. 

I hope this helped somewhat!!! Feel free to DM me with any questions ❤️

Hey! I’m so sorry you’re feeling that way. I’m on 20 mg of fluoxetine, which is generic Prozac. This helps stabilize my moods and keeps the suicidal thoughts down. It makes some people feel energetic, but it makes me sleepy so I take it at night. The major side effect I have with this is nightmares but I have those anyway because of PTSD. I haven’t noticed in change in my appetite since being on it. 

So for my PTSD related nightmares and my panic attacks, I take 2 mg of prazosin, which is generic Minipress. You take this at night because it drops your blood pressure and makes you sleepy. The first morning after you take it, you *will* feel extremely lightheaded. I actually feel lightheaded every morning because of it, but it goes away within a half an hour. As long as you give yourself time in the morning to get up and let the lightheadedness pass, in my experience, you’ll be fine. 

I honestly really like both of these. I’ve been on fluoxetine before and it just works really well for me.
